Arkansas has two tracked data center facilities, both small by industry standards, and the combined recorded power draw for the state rounds to zero measurable megawatts.

The two facilities, TierPoint Little Rock in Pulaski County and Searcy Information Technologies in Searcy, represent different ownership models. TierPoint is a commercial operator; Searcy Information Technologies is run by the City of Searcy itself. Neither facility's footprint suggests the kind of power density associated with AI training or large-scale inference workloads. TierPoint Little Rock is listed at 9,000 square feet, a figure well below what hyperscale AI infrastructure typically requires. No square footage is recorded for the Searcy facility.

The data does not include power capacity figures for either site, which is why the state total reads as zero rather than as genuinely zero. That gap in the record limits what can be said about Arkansas as a compute location. What the data does confirm is that no large announced AI-oriented facility appears here as of the generation date, placing Arkansas outside the current geography of grid-constrained AI buildout.
